title: A Turtle Can Go Five Months Without a Breath Under the Ice

scenes.text: This turtle can go five months without taking a breath.
When a pond freezes, a painted turtle sinks to the bottom and waits in the mud at three degrees.
No air. No oxygen. In lab tests, adults survived over four months like this. Some, five.
Your brain dies in minutes without oxygen. The turtle's metabolism drops to a tenth of normal.
Burning sugar without oxygen makes acid. The turtle dissolves its own shell to neutralise it. A built-in antacid.
In spring it swims up, takes a breath, and rebuilds its shell. Five months. One breath.

description:
The painted turtle is the most oxygen-tolerant air-breathing vertebrate known. Submerged in oxygen-free water at 3 degrees Celsius, adults survived an average of 126 days in Brown University experiments, some more than 150 days, about five months.
Its metabolism falls to about a tenth of normal, and the lactic acid that builds up is neutralised by calcium and magnesium carbonates released from its shell and skeleton, which also store the lactate until spring.
What is the longest you have held your breath?
subject: painted turtle
first_comment: Hatchlings can only manage about 40 days of this, because their soft shells hold almost no minerals to neutralise the acid. What is the longest you have held your breath?
